title: Zodiacally Ephemeris: a table-driven JPL DE440 ephemeris for astrological software
description: Source-available JavaScript ephemeris for astrological software (Node.js): apparent geocentric ecliptic longitudes and speeds of the Sun, Moon, Mercury to Pluto, Chiron and the true lunar node for 1899–2101, built from NASA/JPL DE440s and, for Chiron, the JPL Horizons orbit solution JPL#171, with IAU 2006 sidereal time and Placidus and whole-sign houses. The Chebyshev tables reproduce directly computed apparent places to about 0.5 mas at dense check points (largest error found 0.5002 mas); a rebuild from public JPL data reproduced them byte-identically on macOS/arm64 and numerically equivalently (within 0.00000002″) on Linux x86-64. The repository contains a reproducible benchmark against the Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 and NASA/JPL Horizons, and a technical note (docs/technical-note.md). Free for any use, including commercial, with the attribution line in every reading or result shown or delivered to others; white-label licence without attribution: €690 one-time plus VAT where applicable. Not an OSI open-source licence: the attribution is required, and the engine may not be published or distributed as a standalone library (see LICENSE.txt).
